intro: Reusable building blocks extracted from my own N79 apps (RetroTele, RetroSend, RetroTorch) and from the toolchain used to build them. Each repo is public on GitHub. The status line says what was checked on a real Nokia N79 and what was only run on a PC.

repos.name: telegram-call-engine-c
repos.tagline: Portable C89 engine for Telegram voice and video calls
repos.purpose: The call core of RetroTele: Telegram call library 2.7.7 media plane (ICE over the reflector, encrypted transport, RTP/Opus, H.264 RTP, RTCP) plus the older 2.4.4 protocol. No sockets, clock, threads, malloc or floating point inside: you feed it datagrams and a clock.

status.text: 2.7.7 voice carried real calls on a Nokia N79 with the official Telegram apps (RetroTele 0.12.0). Legacy 2.4.4 voice worked only against clients that still ship it.
Host unit and simulation tests pass with ASan and UBSan.
Video was used on the N79 in RetroTele 0.14.x but only lightly tested; quality is modest.
No group calls, TURN/TCP or IPv6. Needs your own Telegram api_id/api_hash. Not affiliated with Telegram.

repos.name: localsend-py22
repos.tagline: LocalSend protocol v2 client and server in pure Python 2.2
repos.purpose: Send and receive files and text with the LocalSend app from Python for S60 1.4.5. It is the protocol core of RetroSend, with a PyS60 socket backend, a PC backend, tests and a command line example.

status.text: Protocol logic tested on a PC (Python 2.7) against fake peers; Python 2.2 syntax checked.
The same code is used in RetroSend on a real N79. This extracted copy was not re-run on a phone.
No TLS/HTTPS. Other phones untested.

repos.name: symbian-torch-pyd
repos.tagline: torchhw: native PyS60 module for the camera LED torch and phone lights
repos.purpose: A .pyd extension for Python for S60 1.4.5 that controls the camera LED as a steady torch, the HWRM lights (display, keypad) and ECam flash modes. It is the native part of RetroTorch and a small example of a PyS60 module that talks to asynchronous Symbian services.

status.text: LED video light, keypad light and extra light verified on a Nokia N79 inside RetroTorch. The rebuild from this repository was built but not re-run on the phone.
Other S60 3rd Edition phones untested; S60 5th Edition and PyS60 2.x not supported.

repos.name: symbian-s60v3-toolchain
repos.tagline: Symbian C++ toolchain for S60 3rd Edition FP2 on modern Linux
repos.purpose: GnuPoc, GCCE 3.4.3, the S60 3.2 SDK and the PyS60 1.4.5 SDK plug-in, set up by one script, to build native Symbian programs and PyS60 .pyd modules on a current x86_64 Linux. The original archives are kept in its Releases.
repos.license: MIT for the scripts and docs; the bundled third-party archives keep their own licences

status.text: Tested on Manjaro Linux (host GCC 16). It is a build toolchain, so there is nothing to run on the phone itself.
FP2 phones only (for example N79). FP1 phones need the FP1 SDK.

repos.name: symbian-unlock-guide
repos.tagline: Step-by-step guide to unlocking Symbian phones with EasyHackKit 2.0
repos.purpose: Personal, repeatable walkthrough for removing Platform Security restrictions so an old Nokia can install unsigned apps again, with device notes, troubleshooting and a glossary.
repos.license: No licence file in the repository

status.text: Written for my own Nokia N79 (S60v3 FP2) and N82 (S60v3 FP1). Other phones: see the compatibility table in the guide.

repos.name: mtproto-py22
repos.tagline: Telegram MTProto 2.0 client library for Python 2.2 / PyS60
repos.purpose: The network and crypto layer of RetroTele: DH key exchange, encrypted requests, TL serializer, SRP two-factor login and a client (chats, sending, files, updates), in pure Python 2.2, plus an optional native crypto module (tgnative) that is far faster on the phone.
repos.language: Python 2.2 (plus C for the native module)

status.text: The whole stack runs on a real N79 in daily use in RetroTele: login with code, 2FA, chats, sending, files, updates.
Unit tests pass on a PC (Python 2.7); a static checker confirms Python 2.2 compatibility.
The example script in the repo was never run live against Telegram. Python 3 does not work; other phones untested. You need your own api_id/api_hash. Not affiliated with Telegram.

repos.name: opus-symbian-s60
repos.tagline: Opus 1.3.1 fixed-point for Symbian S60 3rd Edition
repos.purpose: Build scripts and config that produce the Opus codec as a static library (tgopus.lib) with GnuPoc and GCCE 3.4.3, with no patches to Opus, plus a self-test and benchmark. Made for RetroTele voice calls.

status.text: Self-test passed and the benchmark ran on a real N79, where Opus then carried real Telegram voice calls. The N79 timings (5.6 / 7.7 / 11.5 ms per 20 ms frame, encode plus decode) come from notes; the raw log is gone.
Rebuilt from the repo layout and the host test passes.
Other S60 3rd Edition phones untested.

repos.name: symbian-s60v3-media-notes
repos.tagline: Camera, H.264 and VoIP audio findings for the Nokia N79
repos.purpose: What the N79's multimedia stack really does: camera, H.264 (DevVideo) and full-duplex VoIP audio, with error codes, needed capabilities and the small native helper programs used to find out.

status.text: Measurements come from a real N79 (notes from RetroTele development; raw logs not included).
All six helpers were rebuilt from this layout and compile and link; they were not re-run on a phone from it.
Needs a hacked (unlocked) phone with Open4All: the helpers use MultimediaDD, which a self-signed package cannot get on a stock phone. Only the N79 was used; other phones untested.

repos.name: pys60-toolbox
repos.tagline: PyS60 1.4.5 toolbox: memory-card install fix and Python 2.2 checkers
repos.purpose: rscfix, a tiny installer-run program that lets a PyS60 app work when installed on the memory card, two checkers that catch Python 2.2 syntax and integer traps, and notes on Python 2.2 and PyS60.

status.text: rscfix verified on a N79 with the app on the memory card; shipped in RetroSend, RetroTorch and RetroTele. The rebuild from this layout compiles but was not re-installed on a phone.
rscfix does not work on a stock phone: it needs an unlocked phone (Open4All). Other phones untested.
